about.job.text: The road pays, if you know where to stand on it.
I take what the road owes me. Keep walking and it won't be yours.
I walk to the shrine and back, and every mile is a prayer.
My feet are sore and my heart is light. The saints keep the road.
Letters, news, the reeve's summons: I carry them all, and I don't read them. Mostly.
Two towns a day if the road is dry. The news goes stale faster than bread.
My mule knows the road better than I do. I just keep the load tied down.
Sacks one way, barrels the other. A cart that rides empty is money lost.
Needles, ribbons, a charm or two. Everything a village forgets to make.
I go where the market isn't. Folk pay for what they can't walk to.
Every cart pays at the bar. The lord keeps the road, the road keeps me.
Coin first, then the bar goes up. I've heard every excuse there is.
I keep the house: the hearth swept, the larder full, the beds aired.
A good house runs quiet. If you notice me, something's gone wrong.
I came out here for the quiet. The quiet has been good company.
The town has its bells. I have the wind and the birds.
We keep the hours: prayer, work, and prayer again. The walls keep the rest.
Copying, gardening, the sick at the gate. There's always work for the brothers.
I collect what's owed to the lord. Nobody is glad to see me, and I don't blame them.
The lord's dues, the lord's peace. I ride the domain and keep both.
